doc.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024

title: Why composing is the hardest place
summary: She finds composing hard because each piece is a fresh start alone, unlike performing with others, and seeks balance between the two.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Okay here’s a quote from you. It started out you were talking about being an instrumentalist, a saxophonist and an educator. But you focused on composing and you said the essence of being a composer is the deepest, hardest place I go in my life. And can you tell me why it’s hard? Why is it — I mean from speaking —

Oh, I think it’s hard because I have to start fresh all the time. It’s like a new start every time I compose, as opposed to performance where I’m kind of revisiting a rhythm, a rhythmic activity in a way, and not that composing isn’t but I’m in the now with other people as opposed to composition where I’m having to get into the now with myself. And I think there’s a really big difference from the act of the two things. There’s similarities but there’s also this, I mean I went through so much isolation the last four years with this. So it’s led me to a place where I’m like, I just want to, I really want to find a balance between performance and composition. Because both of them are good for my soul.
